**Subject: Tuesday reading club – update before the review**

Dear Niamh,

I wanted to give you an update on the Tuesday reading club before the review meeting on Wednesday 18 November. I was sorry to hear in your email of 30 October that the club was to be paused from January because of low attendance and the increase in hall insurance. I know those are real concerns, but the numbers have changed quite a bit, and I hope they might give us reason to reconsider.

We had five children most weeks in September. By mid-October we were up to nine, and last Tuesday, 3 November, we had 14. I’m thrilled to see it taking off. The club has been running since September 2025, from 3.30 to 4.45 on Tuesdays in the meeting room upstairs at Knocknacarra library, and it feels as if the word is finally getting around.

There have been some lovely moments, too. Two sisters from a Ukrainian family joined us in October, and the older girl now reads to her younger sister in English at the end of each session. One boy who wouldn’t open a book in September asked last week if he could take two home. It’s a small thing perhaps, but it meant a lot to see.

We’ve also had a wonderfully generous donation of 120 books from Declan Moran at Salthill Book Nook. They’re mostly for the six-to-nine age group, with a good few as Gaeilge. Between that and the growing attendance, I think it would be a terrible pity to pause the club just as it has found its feet. Could we look at the decision again at the meeting, taking the new numbers into account?

There’s another matter I want to tell you about myself. I met Orla Keane from the Corrib Courier at the farmers’ market, and I got carried away telling her about the club. I said she could “come along any Tuesday”, and she’s interested in visiting with a photographer on Tuesday 24 November.

I should have checked with you first. I was wrong not to, plain and simple. I know the policy is that there can be no photographs of children without your sign-off and the parental consent forms. The coverage could be wonderful for us, but only if it’s done properly.

I’m happy to ring Orla and put the visit on hold until you’ve decided whether it can go ahead. If you do say yes, I can collect the consent forms myself.

Thanks, Niamh. I wanted you to have the full picture before the meeting, and I’d be glad to talk beforehand if that would help.

Warm wishes,  
[Your name]
